name: Ebastine

overview.mechanism: Blocks histamine H1-mediated allergic responses; carebastine is its active metabolite [[EBA-RHINITIS,EBA-RENAL]].
uses: Seasonal allergic rhinitis studied in randomized trials; confirm locally approved indications and product instructions [[EBA-RHINITIS]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled study; 565 participants; four weeks.
rows.intervention: Two oral ebastine regimens, loratadine and placebo.
rows.findings: Both ebastine regimens improved rhinitis symptom scores; the higher regimen improved scores more than loratadine. Overall adverse-event frequency was similar across groups.
rows.limitations: Short symptom trial; efficacy and safety should not be generalized to every allergic condition or long-term exposure.

rows.design: Open-label parallel study; 24 renal-impaired participants (8 each mild/moderate/severe) and 12 healthy controls; five days.
rows.intervention: Ebastine with measured 24-hour creatinine clearance and ECG/laboratory monitoring.
rows.findings: No clinically important exposure, half-life or short-term safety difference was found; between-subject variability was large.
rows.limitations: Small and short; the creatinine-clearance measure must not be replaced with eGFR. This study does not establish a dialysis regimen.

rows.intervention: Ebastine alone, then with ketoconazole; placebo/ketoconazole control.
rows.findings: Ketoconazole increased parent-ebastine AUC 42.5-fold. QTc rose with combination treatment; the incremental rise over ketoconazole alone was not statistically significant.
rows.limitations: Healthy subjects, brief exposure; lack of statistical significance does not prove absence of arrhythmia risk in susceptible patients.

sources.citation: Comparison of once-daily ebastine 20 mg, ebastine 10 mg, loratadine 10 mg, and placebo in the treatment of seasonal allergic rhinitis. PubMed PMID: 10856142.
Pharmacokinetics and safety of ebastine in healthy subjects and patients with renal impairment. PubMed PMID: 17518511.
Co-administration of ketoconazole with H1-antagonists ebastine and loratadine in healthy subjects: pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects. PubMed PMID: 15752381.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

key_interactions.effect: Markedly increases parent-ebastine exposure; QT findings in healthy volunteers cannot establish safety in higher-risk patients [[EBA-KETO]].
key_interactions.action: Check product-specific restrictions before coadministration; do not infer safety from a nonsignificant incremental QTc comparison [[EBA-KETO]].

renal: Small renal-impairment PK data are reassuring but do not replace the current product label or define dialysis dosing [[EBA-RENAL]].
